title: improve-quant-kernels-int8-fp8-smoothquant-dequant-fusion
author: Daniel Kim
description:
Context: Quantized inference is a key lever for cost and throughput. Customers running large-context workloads on Dedicated and Private deployments rely on INT8/FP8 paths. Previous quantized kernels paid extra overhead for dequant/quant boundaries (extra copies, separate kernels) and had suboptimal smoothquant handling, which limited latency and throughput gains in production workloads.

This PR implements a set of targeted kernel and runtime changes to fuse dequantization steps, incorporate smoothquant scaling into fused GEMM kernels, and add a fast path for FP8/INT8 >> float32 consumption that preserves KV cache semantics. The goal is to reduce per-token latency, increase throughput for medium-to-large batches, and reduce memory pressure.

What changed (high level):
- New fused dequantization + GEMM kernels for INT8 and FP8 that apply smoothquant channel scaling inside the kernel to avoid an extra elementwise op and memory copy.
- Introduced a dequant-fusion codepath in the runtime kernel selector and dispatch logic so the fused kernel is preferred when model/quantization metadata matches (per-model quant config).
- KV cache compatibility: the fused kernels operate directly on cached KV buffers with no additional reformatting; added checks to ensure cache alignment on 64B boundaries.
- Scheduling tweaks: continuous batching scheduler updated to prefer fused-quant workers for mixed-precision request queues, reducing stale context switching.
- Fallbacks: runtime falls back to the legacy dequant path if kernel not available or if correctness checks fail; guarded behind a config flag enable_quant_fusion=true for staged rollout.
- Tests and benching: added microbench harnesses (bench/quant/...) and perf-canary jobs to validate latency and throughput across A100/H100.

Implementation notes: all kernel changes are isolated under kernels/quant_fusion/{int8,fp8}.cu with shared helpers. Kernel launch heuristics use model metadata (scale factors from smoothquant) passed from loader; added serialization for these params in the model artifact proto. The runtime selector prefers fused kernels when (1) quant_scheme in model == smoothquant or int8 symmetric and (2) sequence length >= 32 and batch_size >= 1. This keeps overhead low for short-context interactive use.

Benchmarks (perf-canary, A100, seq_len=512 unless noted):
- INT8 fused path: median per-token latency down 28% (from 12.5ms to 9.0ms) and throughput up 35% for batch=8.
- FP8 fused path: median per-token latency down 22% (from 11.4ms to 8.9ms) and throughput up 29% for batch=8.
- End-to-end memory usage: quant path memory down ~18% due to removing temporary dequant buffers.
- Accuracy/regression: end-to-end log-prob delta < 0.5% on held-out eval prompts; added nightly eval to guard regressions.

Compatibility and rollout: Feature gated with runtime config enable_quant_fusion (default off for now). We instrumented metrics (kernel_fusion.accepted, kernel_fusion.fallback_reason) and dashboards in redwood-console for early adopters. Rollout plan: enable for canary fleet -> 10% Dedicated -> 100% after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Why this matters: This reduces operating cost and improves SLOs for customers using quantized inference paths, particularly for medium-to-large batch workloads and long-context scenarios. The fused kernels reduce memory copies and make the smoothquant path competitive with FP32 in latency-sensitive settings.

Notes and caveats: FP8 path still experimental on some older CUDA drivers; tests validate driver capabilities at startup and disable fp8 fusion when drivers are incompatible. We keep the legacy path to ensure no customer-visible correctness changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation (INT8/FP8 fused)
- [x] Runtime selector and dispatch changes
- [x] KV cache compatibility and alignment checks
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Perf benchmarks added to perf-canary
- [x] Metrics + dashboarding
